title: And a fond farewell to “A Gentleman’s Guide to Love and Murder” which...
transcript: alright so I'm gonna do a ranking of the last 10 Tony winners for Best Musical this is actually my 3rd year in a row making this video and the comments make me regret it every time so take a deep breath this is just my opinion it's gonna be okay here we go at No. 10 I have Moulin Rouge I'm a big fan of the movie and unfortunately this adaptation is just not for me at No. 9 I have the outsiders I think it's fine it has some fantastic moments for sure but overall the rest of the shows on this list I just find more exciting artistically number 8 is the one that's gonna make people angry no matter where I put it so here we go I have Dear Evan Hansen a show that I actually do think is widely misunderstood and misinterpreted but I do still think it has issues and I don't think it should have won in 7th place as I've always said I have an immense amount of respect for a strange loop what it's doing what it's saying and I'm very glad that a lot of people resonated with it that it clicked for a lot of people more than it did for me in 6th place I have Kimberly Akimbo I thought this was pretty cute passably charming but didn't do a lot for me beyond that and here I wanna stop and clarify that there's a pretty sizeable gap now on this list between how much I like No. 6 versus No. 5 because next I have the newest winner maybe happy ending which I like quite a bit more than Kimberly Akimbo I'm very much on the hype train for this musical I think it's gorgeous at No. 4 I have Hadestown love it, it's great and as I like to say at every opportunity: underrated book! can you believe that Tootsie won best book over this? and everyone at the time was like “yeah, that makes sense like!” what?! ugh god whatever at No. 3 I have The Band's Visit which I think is a beautiful near-perfect musical an excellent exercise in restraint and I think it deserved pretty much all of the Tonys that it won which is kind of a hot take in 2nd place I have Hamilton which I've said before I'm still struggling with like the burnout and the overexposure but I think with like the 10th anniversary retrospectives I'm starting to get over that and remembering that this is really an astounding work of art despite some legitimate problems with it but in first place I have Natasha Pierre in the Great Comet but at No. 1 still undefeated reigning champ for three years in a row I have Fun Home an emotionally devastating piece of storytelling that even with all of its acclaim, doesn't get enough acclaim
reasoning: The creator places The Outsiders at #9 out of 10 recent Tony winners, calling it 'fine' with 'fantastic moments' but finding the other shows 'more exciting artistically.' This is a lukewarm assessment that neither recommends nor discourages.
